§4Dice So Nice d6 faces Locked

LockedLocked by the owner. The shipped set is dice/final/: six label PNGs (ink baked in) and six bump maps for each of db, dg, ds and dt, plus the flesh and bone textures with their bumps. The viewer below loads exactly those files.

Only faces with a rules effect carry a mark (data/core/dice-pool.yaml); every other face is blank, with an empty label and a flat bump, so each preset still lists six faces. Each bump map is derived in code from its label's alpha, so grooves line up. Each die kind is its own preset with its own colorset, material and baked label ink; the 1 on Gear and Stress dice is violet so it never looks like a 6. Use the face buttons (marked faces carry a diamond) to turn a die to a face, or Roll to pick a random face for every die (no physics). Materials are three.js approximations of the Dice So Nice ones.

drag or arrow keys to turn
Base: bone
Gear: gunmetal
Stress: wax red
Titan: flesh

Per-kind presets, faces and materials

One dice3d.addDicePreset per die kind (d6 shape), each naming its own colorset and listing six baked label files and six bump maps (dice/kinds/<kind>/). Ink is baked into the label files, because Dice So Nice's labelComposite tint recolours every image label on a die with one colour; per-face colours exist only for Dice Library dice. The colorsets keep labelComposite source-over. On Gear and Stress dice the 1 is signal-flare violet #D4A8FF (the Survey Corps emergency flare colour), so a 1 never looks like a 6: 3.4:1 on the gunmetal body (6.8:1 as the metal renders), 4.4:1 on wax red, and a CIEDE2000 difference of 50 from brass and 39 from parchment.

§5Notes and prompts

  • Retry: Fly and Dodge first came back as detailed anime figures (faces, belts, cloak folds) that turned to mush at 32 px. The retry asked for solid pictograms like Rally's and bigger glyphs; the retries are shown. First attempts are kept in art-src/style-lock/rejected/.
  • The ACTION frame came back as a regular pentagon, not the home-plate shape with vertical sides that the prompt asked for. It is consistent across all four icons and distinct from every website frame. Approve it as drawn, or ask for the home-plate shape.
  • Nape strike: the trigger handle reads a little like a spray gun at 128 px. At 32 px it reads as a blade biting the nape.
  • Down at 24 px: the prone figure is thin. The red chevron and the ground line carry the meaning.
  • Codex returned icons at 1254 px. The icons/ copies are resized to 1024 px, with alpha kept.
  • Dice face 6 is the Codex engraving, normalised in code. A version derived straight from brand-emblem.webp is kept in dice/candidates/ as a fallback. It sits on face 6 of the base, Gear and Stress dice; the Titan Die never carries the Wings.
  • Materials: bone uses plastic plus a faint procedural bone grain; Gear uses metal; Stress uses pristine (a matte base under a hard clear coat, which reads as lacquered sealing wax); the Titan Die uses pristine too, because its rough base reads as skin and its clear coat as a wet sheen. Dice So Nice has no subsurface material, so the translucency lives in the flesh texture (cool, bloodless patches and veins); the viewer adds a warm sheen as a stand-in.
  • The flesh and bone textures are procedural (dice/make_textures.py), built from periodic noise so they tile without a seam, each with its own bump map.
  • Preset type ids (db, dg, ds, dt) are proposals; they must match the denominations of the system's DiceTerm classes when those are written.
  • Pips are gone: blank faces carry an empty label and a flat bump (dice/d6-blank-*), so every preset lists six label and bump entries.
  • Label contrast: each kind has its own success ink (dark ink on bone, brass on gunmetal, parchment on wax red, dark oxblood on flesh), and the 1 on Gear and Stress dice is signal-flare violet. Inks are baked into dice/kinds/<kind>/ label files by make_dice.py.
  • Dice locked: Gear 1 is the first cracked cog draw, Stress 1 the first fracture draw, Titan 5 and 6 the fang ring (bite B1). The other candidates (snapped blade, cracked head, grin, eye, first bite, the cog, fracture and bite redraws) stay on disk only.
Action icons, first run action-icons.txt
Use the `board-game-icon-assets` skill for this task (read its SKILL.md and references/icon-principles.md first and follow them). Use your built-in image generation tool to create 4 stamp icons for a tabletop RPG website, one image per icon, and copy each generated PNG into `icons/` inside the current working directory with the exact filename listed (copy the file; do not re-encode, crop, or resize). Do not write code and do not review anything; only generate and copy images. Generate the first icon to lock the frame, stroke, and ink texture, then generate every following icon using the previously generated icons as the visual reference, keeping the frame geometry, stroke weight, canvas margin, and stamp texture identical within each family and across the set. When done, reply with the list of saved absolute paths and one line per icon naming its glyph.

COPY GUARD: copy only the exact file paths your own image generation calls returned in this session. Never copy the newest file in ~/.codex/generated_images, which other sessions running in parallel also write to.

Aspect ratio 1:1 (1024x1024).

REFERENCE IMAGES: the attached colour plates are world reference only (what Survey Corps soldiers, ODM gear, wire, and blades look like), not how to render. The attached stamp icons are approved icons from this same set: match their stroke weight, canvas margin, ink colour, rough stamp edge, and speckle texture exactly. Do not copy their frames or glyphs; this family has its own frame, defined below.

ICON SYSTEM (locked for every icon):
- Stamp icons printed like a rubber stamp or a woodcut: ink on paper. One ink, iron-gall brown-black #29241D, plus one accent, wax-seal red #8B2A21, used sparingly and never as the only cue.
- Bold, chunky, flat shapes; one thick consistent stroke of about 7 percent of canvas width; slightly rough, broken stamp edges with a faint ink speckle inside the solid areas. No gradients, no shading, no 3D, no glow, no drop shadows, no perspective: flat front-on view.
- Square 1024x1024 canvas. The icon is centred and its frame fills a shared safe area: the outer edge of every frame sits exactly within the central 84 percent of the canvas (8 percent empty margin on each side), and every frame of the same family is the same size.
- Background: transparent with true alpha. If transparency is not available, a plain flat pure white #FFFFFF background with nothing else on it (no paper texture, no shadow, no vignette).
- Must stay readable at 32 px: one large simple glyph per icon, at most two or three identifying details, no hairlines, no tiny counters or gaps, generous space between the glyph and the frame.
- No text, letters, numerals, or logos anywhere.
- No electronics shapes: no computer chips, pin tabs, circuit traces, or modern machine parts. The world is pre-industrial.

GLYPH RULES:
- The glyph fills about 65 to 70 percent of the frame's inner area and is built from big solid shapes, with lines at least as thick as the frame stroke. Smaller or outline-only glyphs collapse at 32 px.
- Hands and creatures are one clean solid pictogram silhouette, never knuckles, nails, or wrinkles.
- No plus signs or cross shapes, in red or in ink. Show "more" with an upward double chevron.
- Human pictograms are Survey Corps soldiers: a hooded cloak and two blades held low. Never a medieval knight, sword, or round shield.
- Titan pictograms are lanky humanoids with a slightly too-large head, never a gorilla or golem shape.
- ODM blades are the anime's long, perfectly straight, uniform-width steel strips with an oblique squared tip, divided into snap-off segments by diagonal score gaps like a box-cutter blade, on a chunky pistol-like trigger handle with a trigger guard. No crossguard or pommel, never medieval swords or katanas. A bare "blade" becomes a medieval sword.
- A curved line low inside a frame reads as a smiling mouth. Draw marks as straight diagonals.
- Arrows are bold solid shapes: a shaft at least as thick as the frame stroke and a big triangular arrowhead.

FRAME (new, fixed for this family):
- ACTION frame: a thick ink upright pentagon shaped like a home-base plate turned point-up: a flat horizontal bottom edge, two straight vertical sides rising to about 55 percent of the frame height, and two straight edges meeting in one sharp point at the top centre, with the same stroke as the approved icons and slightly softened corners. Used by Action Catalog entries (the actions and rolls a soldier takes). It must not look like a shield (point at the bottom), an arch (round top), a warning triangle, a diamond, a square, or a ring. The glyph sits in the lower, wider part of the pentagon, centred about 8 percent below the frame's centre. Every icon in this family uses the identical pentagon, same size and position.

ICONS (generate in this order; the first one locks the frame):
1. FILENAME: action-nape-strike.png
   Meaning: Nape strike, the killing cut to the back of a Titan's neck, taken from its Blind Spot with a Blade Set (Strength).
   Glyph: the back of a Titan's head and neck in profile, facing left, as one solid ink silhouette that fills the right half of the glyph area (a big round skull, a thick neck), and one long straight ODM blade (segmented strip on a trigger handle, handle at the upper left) slicing diagonally down from the upper left into the back of the neck. A bold wax-seal red wedge-shaped gash where the blade bites into the nape. Directional cue: the blade itself is the arrow, driving down and to the right.
2. FILENAME: action-fly.png
   Meaning: Fly, moving on ODM Gear wires (Agility).
   Glyph: a small solid soldier pictogram (hooded cloak streaming behind, two blades held low) swinging forward and upward on one taut straight wire that runs from the soldier up to the upper right, and one big bold arrow that sweeps in a rising curve from the lower left under the soldier up to the right, with a wax-seal red arrowhead pointing up and to the right. Directional cue: up and to the right.
3. FILENAME: action-dodge.png
   Meaning: Dodge, a reaction that makes a Titan's or a foe's attack miss (Agility).
   Glyph: a small solid soldier pictogram (hooded cloak, two blades held low) leaning hard to the left in a sideways leap, and one bold arrow that starts at the right, runs toward the centre, then kinks sharply and turns away to the upper left above the soldier, with a wax-seal red arrowhead pointing up and to the left. On the right, a big blunt solid Titan hand (one simple pictogram shape) swiping into the empty space the soldier just left. Directional cue: away, to the left.
4. FILENAME: action-rally.png
   Meaning: Rally, steadying a shaken comrade and clearing their Stress Response (Empathy).
   Glyph: two solid soldier pictograms: a standing soldier on the left reaching down with one arm and gripping the raised hand of a kneeling comrade on the right, pulling them up; above their joined hands, a bold wax-seal red upward double chevron. Directional cue: up.

EXCLUSIONS: no text, no letters, no numerals, no logos, no plus signs, no crosses, no medical symbols, no swords, no shields, no hearts, no stars, no paper texture behind the icon, no background colour.

Foe plate: Bandit plate-foe-bandit.txt
REFERENCE IMAGES: the attached images are approved plates from this same set. Match their rendering exactly: the same anime linework, painterly anime shading, muted warm palette, and level of stylisation. Do not copy their subjects.

Use your built-in image generation tool to create exactly ONE image, then copy the generated PNG into the current working directory, using only the exact file path your own image generation call returned in this session (never the newest file in ~/.codex/generated_images, which other sessions also write to), under the filename given below (copy the file; do not re-encode, crop, or resize it). Do not create or modify any other files, do not write code, and do not review anything. When done, reply with only the absolute path of the saved file.

FILENAME: plate-foe-bandit.png
Aspect ratio 4:5 (for example 1024x1280).

STYLE (locked, colour plate): Semi-realistic anime illustration, the high-end cinematic version of a premium dark-fantasy military anime, like a still from a theatrical anime film. Characters drawn with clean, confident dark linework and soft painterly anime shading; grounded human anatomy and proportions; accurate costume, leather, and metal equipment detail; detailed hand-painted backgrounds with visible brush texture. Not chibi, not photorealistic, not a 3D render, not Western comic style, not glossy digital concept art. Colour: slightly muted, warm, filmic palette that sits well mounted on aged paper, like a faded colour plate bound into an old field manual. Parchment and dust tones (#E4DCC5), iron-gall ink brown-black shadows (#29241D), deep military green (#2F4B3C), gunmetal steel (#56605F), muted flesh and earth (#B38467), dark cloth green (#16211B), with only a sparing wax-seal red accent (#8B2A21). Lifted blacks, restrained saturation, soft film grain, gentle vignette.

WORLD: a walled, 19th-century-inspired world behind colossal stone Walls fifty metres tall. Survey Corps soldiers wear a short tan cropped field jacket, white shirt, white fitted trousers, dark brown leather harness straps crossing the chest, hips, and thighs, knee-high brown boots, and a hooded dark green cloak with the Wings of Freedom emblem (two overlapping stylised wings, one white and one blue, on a small shield) on the back. Omni-directional mobility (ODM) gear sits at the hips: a steel gas canister and a long rectangular blade scabbard box on each hip, and a compact grappling-hook launcher unit at the lower back.

SUBJECT: a portrait plate of a Bandit, a salvager and deserter who lives outside the Walls. He is not a Survey Corps soldier and wears no Survey Corps uniform, no cloak with an emblem, and no ODM gear.
